questions.stem: A trader sells \(25\) articles and gains a profit equal to the cost price of \(5\) articles. Find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Let CP of each article = \(1\) unit
CP of \(25\) articles = \(25\) units
Profit = CP of \(5\) articles = \(5\) units
SP = CP + Profit = \(25 + 5 = 30\) units
Profit% = \(\frac{5}{25} \times 100 = 20\%\)

questions.stem: By selling \(20\) oranges, a vendor gains the selling price of \(4\) oranges. What is his profit percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Let SP of each orange = \(1\) unit
SP of \(20\) oranges = \(20\) units
Profit = SP of \(4\) oranges = \(4\) units
CP = SP - Profit = \(20 - 4 = 16\) units
Profit% = \(\frac{4}{16} \times 100 = 25\%\)

questions.stem: A shopkeeper sells \(15\) items and his profit is equal to the cost price of \(3\) items. If he sells \(25\) items, what will be his profit?
questions.keySolution:
Profit on \(15\) items = CP of \(3\) items
Profit per item = \(\frac{3}{15} = \frac{1}{5}\) of CP per item
Profit on \(25\) items = \(25 \times \frac{1}{5} = 5\) times CP of one item
Profit = Cost price of \(5\) items

questions.stem: A trader gains the cost price of \(8\) articles by selling \(40\) articles. How many articles should he sell to gain the cost price of \(20\) articles?

To gain CP of \(20\) articles, articles needed = \(\frac{20}{\frac{1}{5}} = 20 \times 5 = 100\) articles

questions.stem: A seller gains \(25\%\) profit. If his profit is equal to the cost price of \(5\) articles, how many articles did he sell?

Total CP = \(n\) units
Profit% = \(25\% = \frac{1}{4}\)
Profit = \(\frac{n}{4} = 5\)
Therefore, \(n = 20\) articles

questions.stem: By selling \(16\) mangoes, a vendor gains the selling price of \(2\) mangoes. If the cost price of each mango is Rs. \(15\), find the selling price of each mango.

questions.stem: By selling \(56\) pens, a stationer gains the cost price of \(14\) pens. If he wants to gain \(40\%\), how many pens should he sell?
questions.keySolution:
Current profit rate = \(\frac{14}{56} = \frac{1}{4} = 25\%\)
Current profit per pen = \(\frac{1}{4}\) of CP per pen
For \(40\%\) profit, profit per pen = \(\frac{2}{5}\) of CP per pen
Let SP per pen remain same
Current SP per pen = CP + \(\frac{1}{4}\)CP = \(\frac{5}{4}\)CP
New CP per pen for \(40\%\) profit = \(\frac{SP}{1.4} = \frac{\frac{5}{4}CP}{1.4} = \frac{5CP}{5.6}\)
Number of pens = \(\frac{5.6}{5} \times 56 \times \frac{4}{5} = 80\)
